p: A park with sculptures scattered in the lush greenery and water.
Machida City Museum of Graphic Arts

The only museum in Japan that focuses on prints. Weekdays 10:00-17:00 (admission is until 16:30) Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays 10:00-17:30 (admission is until 17:00) Closed every Monday and 28 Dec-4 Jan. Fees vary depending on the…
Japanese sword and armor of samurai from the Sengoku period are on display. There is also a life-size replica of a part of the famous Oda Nobunaga's castle.
It's a big library, so if you are looking for some books, you might find it here as it has a wide selection.
A dining establishment with darts, card games, and board games. A nice place to have a party with friends.
A cafe with a twist — there are cats running around that you can play with. Great if you want to play with cats but not raise one long-term.
This place has a wide assortment of games, including bowling, karaoke, billiards, and many arcade games.
People worship the god of learning, Sugawara, at this shrine. In Heian period, Sahara was a scholar.

Live rock music, DJ live sets and dance performances throughout the week.
中町１丁目１８−１５ クローヴビル1F
Live house in Machida. Schedule can be accessed on their website. It is also a music school during weekdays.
Live music and club, depending on the day.
This is a famous and very tasty Hokkaido-style miso ramen shop. The "Oyaji Set" is notable.
A rare ramen made with pineapple.
Spicy ramen is the specialty of this shop.
This is a restaurant specializing in soy sauce dishes, a rarity.
Horsemeat dishes are available at affordable prices.
A yakitori restaurant. All the clerks are friendly and nice. They serve good yakitori and sake.
A cafe where you can enjoy Japanese sweets in a relaxed atmosphere.
All you can eat shabu-shabu and sukiyaki. Ninety minutes of greatness.
